If it’s open to you, you’re way better off making Aaliyah I believe (but I haven’t made Aaliyah and can’t say). If you’re not Jewish, it is a strongly-held policy that changing types of visa (like A2 to A5 which is what you’re describing) should require the applicant (you) to be abroad for a “cool down period” of 12 months. You also I believe are not allowed to start this process while your student visa is still good, and you’re not allowed to overstay your student visa. 🙃🙃🙃 basically the govt wants you out of the country while they process a partner visa.

I would recommend having all the Israeli partner’s papers (and yours) ready to go so you can file the minute you hit the ground in the USA because tracking down my Israeli partner’s parent’s tabu and other random stuff took an unexpected amount of time. Make friends with the AIC website and good luck 💗🫂
